item.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
item.description: arXiv:2610.28792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Baily, Alessandro Danelon

item.title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
item.description: arXiv:2610.29204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together. This discriminant is a hypersurface, parametrized by the logarithmic Horn uniformization. Hurwitz forms of toric varieties yield a degree formula, and a description of leading coefficients. We emphasize applications and computations.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Goertz, Bernd Sturmfels, Simon Telen

item.title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlev\'e equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlev\'e equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Matsumoto

item.title: Derived categories of threefolds near the Noether line
item.description: arXiv:2610.29912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that derived categories of canonical stacks associated to general threefolds in the principal component of the moduli space of canonical threefolds on the refined Noether line are semiorthogonally indecomposable. First we generalize a criterion of Kawatani-Okawa for the indecomposability of derived categories of surfaces of general type to higher-dimensional varieties and stacks. And then we generalize a construction of Kobayashi and Hu-Zhang and a classification result of Coughlan-Pignatelli to the second and third Noether lines to show that our criterion applies to these canonical stacks.
item.dc:creator: Jungkai Alfred Chen, Pedro N\'{u}\~{n}ez

item.title: Germwise singular Fourier--Mukai partnerships
item.description: arXiv:2610.29944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how local behavior on the base controls whether integral transforms induce fully faithful functors or equivalences between singularity categories of proper flat families. By working with \'{e}tale germs, we show (under mild hypotheses) that the loci where this happens are open and are compatible with \'{e}tale base change. Moreover, we give examples, exhibit an autoequivalence of the singularity category which detects regularity of the base, and compute these loci for arithmetic families.
item.dc:creator: Pat Lank

item.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.29977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider, Kostiantyn Tolmachov

item.title: On the gap of thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.30020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an algorithm to compute the gap numbers of log canonical thresholds, anticanonical thresholds, and $\mathbb{R}$-complementary thresholds for surface pairs with a given rational hyperstandard coefficient set. As an example, we compute these gap numbers for a special hyperstandard set that appears in the effective boundedness of $n$-complements for surface pairs.
item.dc:creator: Yang He, Vyacheslav V. Shokurov

item.title: The recent counterexamples to the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman Ulrich problem (2003) and to Hochster's small Cohen-Macaulay conjecture (1973): a survey, with a generalization to arbitrary dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.30027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In September 2026 four preprints and an AI-generated manuscript moved one numerical obstruction from projective geometry to local algebra. For a smooth complex projective surface $Y$ with an ample, globally generated divisor $H$ such that $H^2<\sigma(Y)$, the signature, one obtains in turn: no Ulrich bundles when $H$ is very ample (Anghel, arXiv:2609.02718; extended to every dimension by Lopez, arXiv:2609.06678), answering negatively the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman question of 2003 for sheaves supported on the whole variety; no arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, i.e. section rings without graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules in characteristic zero (Anghel, arXiv:2609.15589); and complete local domains without small Cohen-Macaulay modules, counterexamples to Hochster's 1973 conjecture, if $K_Y\equiv4H$ (Chen, arXiv:2609.24142, proposed) or $\sigma>2H^2$ (OpenAI, released 6 October). We recall the definitions and main statements, and add two things. First, through a finite projection to $\mathbb P^2$ and an identity already present in the OpenAI manuscript, the three obstructions become one variance identity; for surfaces this explains the factor $2$ between the graded bound $\sigma\le H^2$ and the local $\sigma\le2H^2$. Second, we generalize the argument of the OpenAI manuscript to every dimension $m\ge2$, with complete proofs: if $X$ is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $m$ and $H$ an ample, globally generated divisor, a small Cohen-Macaulay module over the completed section ring of $(X,H)$ forces $(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{m-2}\le(m+4)H^m$. Consequently the completed section rings of all Hesse pairs, including the ball quotient of the first preprint, have no small Cohen-Macaulay module, and products of Hesse surfaces with projective spaces give complete local domains with an isolated singularity, of every dimension $\ge3$, without small Cohen-Macaulay modules.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Anghel

item.title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.
item.dc:creator: Jenia Tevelev

item.title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.30069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Halpern-Leistner, Andres Fernandez Herrero, Giovanni Inchiostro, Sara Stephens

item.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors
item.description: arXiv:2610.29065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $\Gamma_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Ormsby

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

item.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Satyajit Guin, Pradip Kumar

item.title: Geometric knowledge spaces, Attention pairing and Architectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.29526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a geometric approach to deriving attention mechanisms and exploring potential new transformer architectures. We begin by formalizing the notions of knowledge worlds and attention pairings, then demonstrate how this framework naturally leads to the architectures of standard attention, causal attention, linear attention, tensor attention, and recurrent neural networks. Finally, we introduce several new geometric spaces that may inspire novel neural network architectures.
item.dc:creator: Shang Xu

item.title: Topological degree of fewnomial maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.29808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the topological degree on the positive orthant of a map $F:\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\mathcal{A}$ of $N=n+k+1$ monomials. This degree is well defined under a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope, which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. We give three formulas for it, all in terms of signs of maximal minors. The first one is a Viro formula: the degree is a signed count of the simplices of a regular triangulation of $\mathcal{A}$ which are positively decorated in the sense of Bihan, Santos and Spaenlehauer. The second one is a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and the third one a sum over the vertices of the polyhedron of the Gale dual system. As a consequence, the degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We also obtain a Descartes rule of signs for the degree and, in the generic case, the upper bound $|\deg F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the largest number of facets of a $d$-polytope with $N$ vertices. This bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsg{\aa}rd, we show that the set of possible degrees is symmetric in $n$ and $k$. Since a nonzero degree forces a positive zero, our formulas give sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity statements for their number.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.29835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.
item.dc:creator: Adler Marques

item.title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
item.description: arXiv:2610.29849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen

item.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
item.description: arXiv:2610.29889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].
item.dc:creator: Elke Neuhaus, Irem Portakal, Luca Sodomaco, Katherine Tung

item.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
item.description: arXiv:2610.29970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.
item.dc:creator: Chenjing Bu, Lucien Hennecart

item.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.30065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Negu\c{t}

item.title: Automorphisms of Plane Curves defined from Chebychev polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2505.01216v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any $d\geq 4$ we determine the automorphism groups of the algebraic curves \[ \mathcal{C}_d : y^d = \varphi_d(x), \] where $\varphi_d(x)$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $d$, defined over a field $k$ with $p:=\operatorname{char}(k) \nmid 2d$. For $d>4$, it is $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, except when $2d=p^r+1$ or $4d=p^r+1$ for some $r\geq 1$. In these cases it is, respectively, $(\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z})\rtimes S_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}\times S_3$. Two ingredients used here are a description of all total inflection points on $\cC_d$, and knowledge of the group of fractional linear transformations that preserve the set of zeros of $\varphi_d$.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian, Jaap Top

item.title: On the complement of nef divisors on projective manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2505.10730v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X'$ be a complex projective manifold, $\dim X'>1$, $Z$ a connected analytic subset of codimension one which is the support of a nef effective Cartier divisor $D$ on $X'$, $X:=X'\setminus Z$. Let $\kappa(D)$ be the Iitaka dimension of $D$. We prove that $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $D$ is abundant and $\kappa(D)=1$. In particular, $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $X$ is a proper fibration over an affine curve.
item.dc:creator: S. Feklistov

item.title: Semisimplicity of conformal blocks
item.description: arXiv:2507.06318v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that braid group representations associated to braided fusion categories and mapping class group representations associated to modular fusion categories are always semisimple. The proof relies on the theory of extensions in non-Abelian Hodge theory and on Ocneanu rigidity. By combining this with previous results on the existence of variations in Hodge structures, we further show that such a braid group or mapping class group representation preserves a non-degenerate Hermitian form and can be defined over some CM number field.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal f\"ur die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelles Journal), 2026
item.dc:creator: Pierre Godfard

item.title: Tiny and Unique: The Lubin-Tate Action at Height $p-1$ from the Minimal Curve with Its Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2509.23428v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be odd and $G' = \mathbb{Z}/p \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/(p-1)^2$ the maximal finite subgroup of the Morava stabilizer group at height $p-1$. Inverse Galois theory produces from $G'$ alone a curve $X$, the unique curve of minimal genus with $\operatorname{Aut}(X) \simeq G'$; its ramification, its field of definition and its equation are consequences of the group, not choices. We prove a $G'$-equivariant equivalence between the deformations of $X$ and Lubin--Tate space, so that the Lubin--Tate action of $G'$ is the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ on deformations of the curve. The proof is a coordinate-free Kodaira--Spencer argument reducing to a single character count. The action becomes explicit: $G'$ acts through $\mathbb{F}_p \rtimes \mathbb{F}_p^\times$ shifting and scaling $p+1$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$. From this we compute $H^*(G', \pi_* E_{p-1})$ and its Tate cohomology. One identity, $\pi^{p-1} = -p$, runs through every section.
item.dc:creator: Rin Ray

item.title: A remark on the Moduli of parabolic connections
item.description: arXiv:2509.24504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the moduli space of stable parabolic connections of full flag type with generic rational weights on a compact Riemann surface $X$ of genus $g \ge 3$, with singularities along the parabolic points. We compute the Chow groups of the fixed determinant moduli space consisting of parabolic connections whose underlying parabolic bundle is stable. We show that the moduli space of stable parabolic connections is not rationally connected, whereas the fixed determinant moduli space is rationally connected and in fact rational. We also prove that the determinant map to the Picard variety is universal among morphisms to abelian varieties. Finally, we show that the algebraic group of rank one holomorphic connections acts trivially on the cohomology of the moduli space of stable parabolic connections.
item.dc:creator: Pradeep Das, Snehajit Misra, Anoop Singh

item.title: A Mapping Theorem for Derived Foliations
item.description: arXiv:2510.21497v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we construct in characteristic zero a derived foliation on derived mapping stacks $\underline{\mathbf{Map}}_S(X,Y)$ under natural representability assumptions, for $S$ a base derived stack, $X$ a proper schematic, flat, and local complete intersection derived stack over $S$, and $Y$ a relative derived Deligne-Mumford stack locally of finite presentation over $S$, when $Y$ is equipped with a derived foliation relative to $S$. In the process, given a derived stack $Z$ locally of finite presentation over a derived stack $X$, we will first show that the $\infty$-category of derived foliations over $Z$ relative to $X$ embeds as a full subcategory of derived stacks over $Z$ equipped with extra structure, and describe its essential image explicitly. We will then show that given a proper schematic, flat, and local complete intersection map of derived stacks $f : X \to Y$, the push-forward or Weil-restriction functor $f_*$ from derived stacks over $X$ to derived stacks over $Y$ preserves the preceding essential images, and thus defines a push-forward, from derived foliations over $Z$ relative to $X$, to derived foliations over $f_* Z$ relative to $Y$, under natural representability assumptions. The aforementioned result on derived mapping stacks is obtained as a special case of this statement. As example applications, given a smooth projective scheme $X$ equipped with a derived foliation, we obtain derived foliations on the derived moduli stacks $\mathbb R \overline{\mathbf M}_{g,n}(X)$ and $\mathbb R \mathbf{Hilb}^{lci}(X)$, which are respectively the derived enhancements of the moduli stack of families of stable curves of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points on $X$, and of the Hilbert scheme of closed subschemes of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Victor Alfieri

item.title: Picard bundles and Twisted Picard bundles on the Jacobian of a curve
item.description: arXiv:2602.19152v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Y$ denote an irreducible projective curve with at most nodes as singularities and defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We study the restriction of the twisted Picard bundles on the compactified Jacobian $\overline{J}(Y)$ of $Y$ to the embedded curve in $\overline{J}(Y)$. As an application, we show that for $g =2$ and each integer $r \ge 3$, there is a two-dimensional family of stable ACM bundles on the compactified Jacobian which has the Picard bundle in its limit. We define an embedding $\alpha_Y$ of the (generalised) Jacobian $J(Y)$ in the moduli space $U^s_Y(n,d)$ of stable vector bundles on $Y$ using a twisted restriction $E_Y$ of a Picard bundle to $Y \subset J(Y)$. We show that (under suitable conditions) the restriction of the universal bundle $\mathcal{U}$ to $Y \times J(Y)$ is stable for suitable polarisation. For the embedding of a smooth curve $Y$ given by $E_Y \otimes B, B$ a line bundle of degree $b$, we show that the restriction of the Picard bundle on $U^s_Y(n, d+nb)$ to $J(Y)$ is $\theta$-semistable for $b \ge 2g-1$ and $\theta$-stable for $b \ge 2g$. We also determine the relation between the restriction of the theta divisor on $U^s_Y(n,d+nb)$ to $J(Y)$ and the theta divisor $\theta$ on $\overline{J}(Y)$.
item.dc:creator: Usha N. Bhosle

item.title: Transitive automorphism groups of maximal curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.17611v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and let $X$ be a maximal curve of genus at least two over $\F_{q^2}$. We prove that the automorphism group of $X$ acts transitively on its rational points if and only if $X$ is the Hermitian curve, or $q=5$ and $X$ is the unique $\F_{25}$-maximal curve of genus $3$, namely the maximal Klein quartic. Together with the result of Giulietti and Korchm\'aros in characteristic two, this gives the classification for every prime power $q$. In particular, the Hermitian curve is the only maximal curve of genus at least two whose automorphism group is doubly transitive on its rational points.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian

item.title: Obstructions to the ampleness of invariant jet differentials on complete intersections
item.description: arXiv:2609.33710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the analogue, for invariant jet differentials, of the principal symbol of a differential operator: the component of maximal degree in the highest derivative. The top symbol identifies a canonical quotient bundle of the Demailly--Semple bundle $E_{k,m}T^*_X$, with values in jet differentials of lower order, and together with the Br\"uckmann--Rackwitz vanishing theorem it gives a non-ampleness criterion for $E_{k,m}T^*_Z$ on complete intersections $Z\subset\PP^N$. On the Demailly--Semple tower the top symbol is the restriction to a thickening of the vertical divisor, inside the singular jets. The criterion applies in orders $3$ and $4$: $E_{3,5q}T^*_X$ is not ample on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^4$, and $E_{4,m}T^*_X$ is not ample for $m\ge7$ with $m\equiv0,1,2\pmod 7$ on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^5$ of degree at least $2$. This contradicts the Diverio--Trapani conjecture at its own threshold.
item.dc:creator: Simone Diverio

item.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional coherent sheaf
item.description: arXiv:2610.21904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles, and let $\mathcal{E}_X$ and $\mathcal{E}_Y$ be exceptional coherent sheaves on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $\mathcal{E}_X^\perp\simeq \mathcal{E}_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.
item.dc:creator: Songtao Kenneth Ma

item.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2411.06497v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.
item.dc:creator: Mathew George

item.title: Exactness property of Breuil-Kisin functors and Bloch-Kato Selmer groups
item.description: arXiv:2603.26035v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field and $T$ a lattice in a semistable representation of $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ with Hodge-Tate weights in $[0, r]$. Assuming $0\leq r<p-1$, we prove that for a semistable extension of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ by $T$, the corresponding sequence of strongly divisible modules is exact. Analogous statements are proved for Breuil-Kisin modules and for prismatic $F$-crystals for all $r\geq 0$. In the crystalline case, we deduce that the integral Bloch-Kato Selmer group $H^1_f(K, T)$ is computed by $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ in the category of crystalline strongly divisible modules. Using further exactness results, we define a tensor product of strongly divisible modules, which commutes with the functors to Galois representations. As an application, we show that for abelian varieties $A_1, A_2$ over $K$ with good reduction, the cup product map $\delta_1\cup\delta_2:A_1(K)\otimes A_2(K)\rightarrow H^2(K, T_p(A_1)\otimes T_p(A_2))$ induced by the Kummer sequences of $A_1, A_2$ factors through an $\mathrm{Ext}^2$ group of strongly divisible modules. In the appendix we generalize further the main exactness results to coherent reflexive $F$-gauges.
item.dc:creator: Pavel \v{C}oupek, Evangelia Gazaki, Adriano Marmora

item.title: Spherical Milnor Spaces II: Projective Quotients and Higher Topological Structures
item.description: arXiv:2605.16370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study projective and semidirect quotients of the spherical Milnor construction and develop a step-by-step lifting obstruction from their explicit spherical local sections. The resulting transition functions produce a twisted Cech 2-cocycle for any specified compatible extension with abelian kernel. When the kernel is $U(1)$ and the sign acts by complex conjugation, taking logarithms yields a twisted Dixmier--Douady obstruction under stated sheaf hypotheses. We identify its projective-operator interpretation when an additional representation is supplied, without attempting a classification of K-theory twists. We also investigate descent of differential-geometric structures and, under restricted-operator hypotheses, Schwinger cocycles and lifting gerbes for loop groups.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Magnot

item.title: Rigidity of multisections to the universal cubic plane curve
item.description: arXiv:2607.14128v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the following question of Farb: For which positive integers n is it possible to choose n distinct points continuously on every smooth cubic plane curve? This paper is a continuation of the work of Banerjee-Chen. We prove that such choice is unique up to homotopy for n=27 (smallest open case), and does not exist for n=36k+18.
item.dc:creator: Jinwen Yao (Tsinghua University)

item.title: An Explicit Belyi Map for the Wiman Sextic and Cusp Forms for a Noncongruence Subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2608.30798v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we explicitly determine an algebraic Belyi function on a unique smooth projective model $\widetilde{W}$ of the Wiman sextic curve $W$ and describe its complex uniformization in terms of modular functions associated with a certain noncongruence subgroup $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}} \subset {\rm SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we give a direct proof of the unbounded denominators conjecture for weight $2$ cusp forms with respect to $\Gamma_{\widetilde{W}}$. The conjecture is now known in full generality by the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang, following earlier progress including work of Dong, Lin, and Ng. Our proof, however, uses a degeneration of $\widetilde{W}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{5}$ together with explicit Puiseux series expansions and is substantially different from the methods employed in their work.
item.dc:creator: Madoka Horie, Takuya Yamauchi

item.title: Relative $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and $p$-adic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.08179v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be an affinoid rigid analytic space over a $p$-adic field, equipped with a suitable \'etale map to a unit polydisk. We provide a formalism of \emph{imperfect relative period rings} over $X$, which lie inside the corresponding perfect relative period rings constructed by Kedlaya--Liu. Then we establish a relative version of the Fontaine--Cherbonnier--Colmez equivalence between $p$-adic local systems on $X$ and \'etale $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules over such imperfect relative period rings, generalizing previous works of Andreatta--Brinon and others. Using this equivalence, we construct $p$-adic differential equations attached to de Rham local systems, carrying both geometric and arithmetic differential operators. This generalizes the work of Berger to the relative geometric setting. Along the way, we study a relative Fontaine--Sen theory on the decompletion of $\Gamma$-modules over the relative $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-period rings.
item.dc:creator: Hansheng Diao, Yong Suk Moon, Zijian Yao

item.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.23822v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.
item.dc:creator: Kyobeom Song

item.title: Lie weights for CM curves and unipotent Selmer dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.12013v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an equidistribution result for Galois characters in the graded Lie components $L_n$ associated to the $\mathbf{Q}_p$-fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve $X$ over a number field $k$ with geometrically CM Jacobian. That is, we consider the $p$-adic completion of a fixed character lattice, where we define measures $\mu_n$ counting normalized character multiplicities in $L_n$, and show that $(\mu_n)_n$ weakly converges to the Haar measure. The key idea to prove convergence is to write the Fourier coefficients of $\mu_n$ in terms of traces of operators on $L_n$ induced by symplectic operators on the Tate module, and control them with a known symplectic character formula, followed by Weyl's criterion for compact abelian groups. Our main arithmetic application is to combine equidistribution with the Iwasawa-theoretic method of Coates--Kim and a compactness argument for moving analytic loci, giving a dimension inequality for unipotent Selmer schemes: $\dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}H^1_f(G_{k,T},U_n)< \dim_{\mathbf{Q}_p}\prod_{v\mid p}H^1_f(G_v,U_n)$ for all sufficiently large $n,$ with the quotient having limit superior at most $1/2.$ This answers a particular case of a conjecture by Kim, from which the finiteness of $X(\mathbf{Q})$ can be recovered when $k=\mathbf{Q}.$
item.dc:creator: Ander Martin

item.title: A vanishing theorem for finitely supported ideals in regular local rings
item.description: arXiv:math/0702082v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A cohomological vanishing property is proved for finitely supported ideals in an arbitrary d-dimensional regular local ring. (Such vanishing implies some refined Briancon-Skoda-type results, not otherwise known in mixed characteristic.) It follows that the adjoint of a finitely supported ideal I of order a has order sup(a+1-d, 0), and that taking adjoints of finitely supported ideals commutes with taking strict transforms at infinitely near points. In particular, the adjoint of I is also finitely supported. Also: if this I is a normal ideal, then its reduction number is the least integer > d(1-1/a).
item.dc:creator: Joseph Lipman
